question.problem:
$$
{A}^{T}\,A=[\begin{aligned}13 & -12 \\ -12 & 13\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}{v}_{11} & {v}_{12} \\ {v}_{21} & {v}_{22}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ what is the value of $|{v}_{11}|+|{v}_{21}|?$
question.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ the columns of $V$ must be the right singular vectors of $A,$ i.e., the unit eigenvectors of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$

From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that the singular values are ${\sigma }_{1}=5$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=1.$ So, the first column of $V$ corresponds to the singular value ${\sigma }_{1}=5.$

Hence, we need to find a unit eigenvector of ${A}^{T}\,A$ that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=25.$ Computing ${A}^{T}\,A-25I,$ we get

$$
{A}^{T}\,A-25I=[\begin{aligned}13 & -12 \\ -12 & 13\end{aligned}]-25[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-12 & -12 \\ -12 & -12\end{aligned}]
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-25I)v=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we get 

$$
\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
|{v}_{11}|+|{v}_{21}|=|-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}|+|\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}|=\sqrt{2}.
$$
